summary: The article accurately describes SEBI's newly introduced PRIM route for Portfolio Managers, including the minimum investment, permitted instruments, and how it differs from traditional PMS and direct mutual fund investing. The information is consistent with recent news and regulatory updates.

claims.claim: SEBI has introduced the Portfolio Managers Route for Investing in Mutual Funds (PRIM), offering a new avenue for high-net-worth investors.
claims.note: SEBI approved the introduction of the Portfolio Managers Route for Investing in Mutual Fund units (PRIM) at its 215th meeting.

claims.claim: Under PRIM, SEBI-registered Portfolio Managers can construct portfolios using mutual funds, ETFs, index funds, and SIFs.
claims.note: The framework allows portfolio managers to invest clients' money in direct plans of mutual funds, including ETFs, index funds, and Specialised Investment Funds (SIFs).

claims.claim: This route requires a minimum investment of ₹25 lakhs, making it accessible to a broader segment compared to traditional PMS.
claims.note: The minimum investment for PRIM is ₹25 lakh, which is lower than the ₹50 lakh minimum for conventional PMS.

claims.claim: As with all Portfolio Management Services, PRIM operates under the strict regulatory framework of SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020.
claims.note: SEBI approved the introduction of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2026, which will replace the existing Portfolio Managers Regulations, 2020. PRIM operates under the new 2026 regulations.

claims.claim: Traditional Portfolio Management Services (PMS), which typically require a minimum of ₹50 lakhs.
claims.note: SEBI mandates a minimum investment of ₹50 lakh for all PMS accounts in India, as per the SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020.

claims.claim: Portfolio managers offering PRIM can charge a fixed management fee of up to 1% of a client's assets, while performance-linked fees will also be permitted.
